name: CORRUGATED METAL WORKSHOP
text: This shack is pieced together from rusty
corrugated metal. The orange glow of the tube
light makes the grime look almost warm.

name: CANVAS HAMMOCK SETUP
text: A slung canvas hammock hangs low over the
floor plating. You wonder how anyone sleeps
with that generator humming right next to
them.

name: TANGLED POWER CORDS
text: Heavy black cables snake across the floor
panels. They look thick enough to carry a
serious current from the generator.

name: STUFFED METAL SHELVING
text: The metal shelves are bowing under the weight
of salvaged parts and unlabeled cans.
Everything is covered in a fine layer of dust.

name: WORKBENCH AND COMPUTER
text: The wooden workbench holds a bulky old monitor
and scattered tools. It's set up right by the
window for maximum daylight.

name: LOWER STORAGE SHELVES
text: These lower shelves are packed with more
rusted cans and scrap bins. It looks like a
haphazard filing system for scavenged goods.

name: OVERHEAD CONDUIT PIPE
text: A thick, rusted pipe runs along the upper
wall, feeding down into an electrical box.
It's secured with heavy iron brackets.

name: CONCRETE FLOOR PANELS
text: The entrance has solid concrete flooring,
distinct from the metal grates inside. They
are cracked and worn from heavy boots.

name: LOOPING POWER CABLE
text: A loop of the thick black cable rests near the
generator's base. It's caked with dust from
being dragged across the floor.

name: HANGING TOOL RACK
text: Wrenches and unknown implements dangle from a
makeshift rack on the wall. They are arranged
by size, the only organized thing in the room.

name: PORTABLE GENERATOR UNIT
text: The red generator is the heart of this
workshop, humming loudly. Its control panel is
battered, but the power light is a steady
green.

name: STACKED STORAGE BINS
text: Olive green military-style bins are stacked
precariously near the generator. They look
sturdy enough to hold heavy salvage.

name: RUSTED METAL PLATE
text: A large, rusted metal plate leans against the
wall, partially covering the floor grate. It
looks like it was scavenged from a larger
vehicle.

name: GENERATOR PLUG CABLE
text: This thick orange cord plugs directly into the
generator's main outlet. It looks newer than
the black cables snaking around the floor.
